name: Look up an unfamiliar word form and read its senses
audience: a writer who meets an unfamiliar word while drafting text on a Linux desktop
objective: From a typed word form, reach the headword entry and read its part-of-speech sections with definitions and examples, then jump to a related word's entry and come back.
workflow: type the word form into the search entry; live search or Enter runs the lookup
read the entry: part-of-speech section header, headword, IPA, numbered senses with a definition and example sentences
click a synonym or related-word button to open that word's entry
return to the starting entry from the history sidebar
acceptance: a typed form such as an inflected or lowercase variant resolves to the headword entry and lists its part-of-speech sections
each sense shows a definition sentence, plus example sentences when the corpus provides them
a no-hit lookup shows 'Did you mean' alternatives instead of an empty result page
clicking a related word opens its entry while the earlier term stays in the history sidebar for return
